quests.question: All safety checks must be completed ___ departure.
quests.hint: This is a formal, more sophisticated version of 'before'.
quests.explanation: 'Prior to' is a formal equivalent of 'before', common in official instructions and procedures.

quests.question: The company's stock price fell sharply ___ the announcement.
quests.hint: This is a formal, more sophisticated version of 'after'.
quests.explanation: 'Following' is a formal equivalent of 'after', commonly used in news and business writing.

quests.question: Please review the attached document ___ our meeting tomorrow.
quests.hint: This asks for something to happen earlier than a scheduled event, in formal register.
quests.explanation: 'Prior to' returns here, the same formal register taught with the safety-check example.

quests.question: The construction team finished the project two weeks ___ schedule.
quests.hint: This describes finishing earlier than planned.
quests.explanation: 'Ahead of schedule' is the fixed idiom for completing something earlier than planned.

quests.question: Due to supply issues, the launch is now running ___ schedule.
quests.hint: This describes falling later than planned, the opposite of the earlier example.
quests.explanation: 'Behind schedule' is the fixed idiom for falling later than planned, the opposite of 'ahead of schedule'.

quests.question: She always likes to stay ___ the curve when it comes to new technology.
quests.hint: This is a fixed idiom for staying more advanced than current trends.
quests.explanation: 'Ahead of the curve' is a fixed idiom meaning more advanced or informed than general trends.

quests.question: All employees must badge in at the main entrance, ___ next Monday.
quests.hint: This marks a formal starting point for a new rule that hasn't taken effect yet.
quests.explanation: 'As of' marks a formal starting point for a new rule or change, even one that begins in the future.

quests.question: Over ten thousand people had registered for the event, ___ the latest count.
quests.hint: This introduces the most recent point at which a figure was measured.
quests.explanation: 'As of' introduces the most recent point at which a figure was measured or checked.

quests.question: The new pricing takes effect ___ the first of the month.
quests.hint: This marks exactly when a change becomes effective, following the same pattern as the earlier examples.
quests.explanation: 'As of' fits again here, marking the exact point when a policy change becomes effective.

quests.question: The team encountered numerous unexpected challenges ___ the course of the project.
quests.hint: This is the fixed word that always pairs with 'the course of'.
quests.explanation: 'Over the course of' is a fixed phrase describing something unfolding gradually across an entire period.

quests.question: The city transformed from a small fishing village into a bustling metropolis ___ the course of several decades.
quests.hint: A gradual transformation is being described across a long stretch of time.
quests.explanation: 'Over the course of' fits again, describing gradual change unfolding across decades.

quests.question: Trust between the two nations was rebuilt slowly ___ the course of many years of diplomacy.
quests.hint: The same fixed phrase from the earlier examples applies here too.
quests.explanation: 'Over the course of' completes the pattern once more, describing gradual change across many years.

quests.question: Tensions were running high ___ the election, with both campaigns making last-minute appeals.
quests.hint: This describes a whole period of building tension, not just the final night before.
quests.explanation: 'In the run-up to' describes an extended period of building tension before an event, unlike 'on the eve of', which refers only to the night just before.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of

quests.question: The bride could hardly sleep from excitement ___ the wedding.
quests.hint: This describes the single night immediately before an event, not a longer build-up period.
quests.explanation: 'On the eve of' refers specifically to the night immediately before an event, distinct from the longer period described by 'in the run-up to'.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of

quests.question: For weeks, the entire town seemed to buzz with anticipation ___ the championship game.
quests.hint: The phrase 'for weeks' points to an extended period, not a single final night.
quests.explanation: 'In the run-up to' fits because 'for weeks' signals an extended lead-up period, not the single night described by 'on the eve of'.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of

quests.question: All contractors must comply ___ local safety regulations at all times.
quests.hint: This links following a rule to the regulation itself.
quests.explanation: 'Comply with' is the fixed idiom for following a rule or regulation.

quests.question: The design needed to conform ___ strict industry standards before approval.
quests.hint: This near-synonym of 'comply with' takes a different fixed preposition.
quests.explanation: 'Conform to' is the fixed idiom meaning to match a standard, taking a different preposition than the near-synonym 'comply with'.

quests.question: Employees are expected to adhere ___ the company's code of conduct.
quests.hint: This links strict compliance to the standard being followed.
quests.explanation: 'Adhere to' is the fixed idiom for strictly following a rule, policy, or standard.

quests.question: Please refrain ___ using your phone during the performance.
quests.hint: This links holding back from an action to the action itself.
quests.explanation: 'Refrain from' is the fixed idiom for deliberately not doing something.

quests.question: As part of the health study, participants were asked to abstain ___ alcohol for a month.
quests.hint: This links deliberately avoiding something to the thing being avoided.
quests.explanation: 'Abstain from' is the fixed idiom for deliberately avoiding something, often for health or moral reasons.

quests.question: After a long week, she finally allowed herself to indulge ___ a slice of chocolate cake.
quests.hint: This is the opposite idea of the earlier examples — allowing yourself something, not avoiding it.
quests.explanation: 'Indulge in' means allowing yourself a pleasure, the opposite idea of 'refrain from' and 'abstain from', and it takes a different preposition.

quests.question: He's been so preoccupied ___ work lately that he's barely seen his family.
quests.hint: This links someone's distracted attention to what's consuming it.
quests.explanation: 'Preoccupied with' is the fixed idiom for being so focused on something that little else gets attention.

quests.question: She became completely engrossed ___ the novel, losing all track of time.
quests.hint: This describes being fully absorbed inside an activity.
quests.explanation: 'Engrossed in' is the fixed idiom for being completely absorbed in an activity.

quests.question: The whole team was immersed ___ the final stages of the project when the news broke.
quests.hint: This follows the same pattern as the previous example — total absorption in an activity.
quests.explanation: 'Immersed in' follows the same pattern as 'engrossed in', describing total absorption in a task.

quests.question: Completely oblivious ___ the chaos around him, he continued reading his book.
quests.hint: This links a lack of awareness to its surroundings.
quests.explanation: 'Oblivious to' is the fixed idiom for being completely unaware of something happening around you.

quests.question: The senator seemed strangely indifferent ___ the concerns raised by his constituents.
quests.hint: This links a lack of interest or concern to the issue itself.
quests.explanation: 'Indifferent to' is the fixed idiom for showing no interest or concern toward something.

quests.question: In modern usage, the brand's name has become almost synonymous ___ quality.
quests.hint: Unlike the two previous examples, this word takes a different fixed preposition.
quests.explanation: 'Synonymous with' is the fixed idiom for describing something so closely associated with a quality that the two seem equivalent.

quests.question: A quiet, well-lit workspace is more conducive ___ concentration than a noisy open-plan office.
quests.hint: This links a favorable condition to the result it helps produce.
quests.explanation: 'Conducive to' is the fixed idiom for describing conditions that help produce a particular result.

quests.question: Older buildings in this region are particularly prone ___ flooding during heavy rains.
quests.hint: This links a tendency toward a negative outcome to that outcome itself.
quests.explanation: 'Prone to' is the fixed idiom for having a tendency toward a particular problem or outcome.

quests.question: Some risk is inherent ___ any major business decision, no matter how carefully it's planned.
quests.hint: Unlike most of the words in this unit, this one takes a different fixed preposition.
quests.explanation: 'Inherent in' is the fixed idiom for describing a quality built into the very nature of something, closing this unit with a useful exception to the 'to' pattern.
